scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw DFT outputs is infeasible in verifier sandbox; structural ordering of barriers and adsorption energy range are the paper's own verifiable claims.

hidden_assets.purpose: adsorption energy range and inequality rules
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from paper: styrene adsorption energy ~1.00 eV; ordering: interdimer H-abstraction (r2) is the lowest barrier among H-abstraction pathways and lower than OH-abstraction.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Adsorption range 0.8-1.2 eV set to allow DFT code variations while excluding nonsensical values; inequalities enforce the paper's reported trend.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's actual conclusions; the range is based on the reported value with generous margin.

outputs.description: Activation barriers and adsorption energy for styrene on water-saturated Si(100)-(2×1) zigzag surface. Contains only the five required rows: adsorption, r1_Habstraction, r2_Habstraction, r3_Habstraction, r2_OHabstraction.

output_contract.notes: The checker verifies relative ordering: r2_Habstraction < r1_Habstraction, r2_Habstraction < r3_Habstraction, r2_Habstraction < r2_OHabstraction, and checks that the adsorption energy is positive and in the range [0.8, 1.2] eV. No O‑adatom rows or checks are required.

steps.description: Structural audit: inequalities r2<r1, r2<r3, r2<r2_OH and adsorption energy in [0.8,1.2] eV.
